# Arpit Maheshwari — Product & Design Leader, AI & Data-Intensive Products

> Product designer specialised in human-in-the-loop design for AI products — the surface where a person
> decides to act on a model's output. Sixteen years, five industries. Fully remote from Indore,
> India (GMT+5:30) with 4–5 hours of daily US East Coast overlap. Available · 4 weeks' notice.
> Looking for one role: founding product & design lead at an AI product company of 5–40 people, or a
> staff / director seat where human-in-the-loop design is the job.

Thesis: "Your model is right. Your users still won't bet on it." The gap between a correct
answer and an acted-on one is a design problem — evidence beside the number, abstention instead
of bluffing, overrides that become training signal, confidence bound to an action.

He designs AND ships: the front-end of features he designed goes out in the PR under his name.
This site is hand-built as the receipt (source: https://github.com/arpitmaheshwari).

## Receipts (verified metric strings)

- AdTech — Talon Outdoor (named client, publicly documented): an ad agency became the market’s aggregator — six systems, one platform (Plato trading, Ada audience intelligence, creative management, play reporting, free media-owner inventory SaaS, white-label franchisor booking) under one design system, later ported into Claude · campaign planning 2 wks → 3 hrs once traders started betting on the algorithm ·
  £69,000 average media-value gain per client · 45% less time and effort to plan and book a campaign
- FinTech · AI-assisted private equity (NDA): deal screening 60% faster · measured pre- vs post-rollout
- VC/PE · technical due diligence (NDA): diligence cycle 3 wks → 4 days · 16 analysis dimensions, a finding became a signal only at sufficient confidence
- EdTech · PTC University (public): product definition + quarterly roadmap 2016–2019 ·
  150k active learners migrated onto one platform in 24 months · $1M / yr print savings · subscription 0% → 64% of new
  bookings (Q3 2017 → Q3 2018) · 550k+ registered learners · 5 → 1 platforms · 9 → 11 locales
- Telecom · Telefónica MyO2 & Priority Moments (public): 4M+ users · designed and coded via
  Equal Experts, 2012–14 (launch-era figures are O2's public record)
- Consumer · PlanIt (public product, since deprecated): a London transit app · 0 usability complaints to customer
  service in the launch window · 1,000 unique visitors / 250 active users per month (small, and always stated as
  small) · shipped with no tutorial; users from teens to eighty-somethings navigated unaided · Jul–Dec 2021
- Org tooling · OrgOS (NDA): designed for 200 people coordinating with 0 managers · 8 modules · in use by 250 people today (2026)

## The seven case theses (each case proves one stealable principle)

1. AdTech · Talon Outdoor: "Users don't adopt the most accurate system. They adopt the one that lets them argue back."
2. FinTech · PE screening: "A score is a claim. Experts don't buy claims — they buy claims with references."
3. VC/PE · technical diligence: "Remove the wrong friction and you get speed. Add the right friction and you get a verdict someone will sign."
4. EdTech · PTC University: "Before you redesign the screens, check whether the contract underneath them is the thing that's broken."
5. Telecom · O2 UK: "The trust isn't in the logic underneath. It's in whether the surface gives someone a reason to act."
6. Org design · OrgOS: "When the user base and the org chart are the same people, every design call is an org-design call."
7. Consumer · PlanIt: "When the reason people won’t act is emotional, the interface is where you pay it — not the model."

## Key pages

- [Homepage](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/): positioning, proof, interactive diagnostic
- [The technical screen, pre-answered](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/screen/): a CTO's screening
  questions answered in writing — eval boundaries, abstention thresholds, ownership scoping
- [The Lab — code as the deliverable](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/lab/): loop.js, a
  zero-dependency ES module implementing the trust-pattern decision logic (Act/Review/Ignore,
  calibration scoring via Brier score and expected calibration error, abstention policy, latency
  disclosure) with 42 tests that run in-browser and under Node; trustlint, a deterministic linter
  for the shape of an AI answer; and a measured teardown of how this site is built.
- [AI design patterns library](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/patterns/): the design system for
  trusting and governing AI agents — the capability contract draws the system's edges; inside
  them the Act/Review/Ignore rule resolves every score and agent action to one verb; 8
  production-earned patterns build it out (provenance, calibration, reversibility…)
- [The method](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/process/): the design process in three acts —
  the wager (desirable·feasible·viable), the spiral (Listen→Structure→Prove→Land, loops ending
  in front of a user), and the open loop (shipping as the first honest data)
- [Case studies](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/#featured-case-studies): seven cases, three AI
- [Human in the Loop — the book](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/book/): the same content as an
  interactive monograph with live pattern demos
- [Resources](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/resources/): the AI design checklist, founder questions,
  and the intelligent-systems glossary
- [The design system as a Claude plugin](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/lab/plugin.html): the site's tokens,
  type scale, spacing grid, component grammar and ten ship gates, installable
- [Writing](https://arpitmaheshwari.com/writing/): essays, with shorter pieces on Substack
